messages:
sam: Quick FYI - hit a weird SDK startup issue on Cloudflare Workers while testing sampleapp-edge. Authorization header shows up twice on a single request. Minimal repro available. Anyone seen this?

mira: yup, ran into this too. Looks like esbuild + wrangler ended up bundling both our ESM and CJS runtime chunks because of conditional exports. Both modules run top-level init that attaches auth, so headers get duplicated.

kevin: is it duplicated headers on the same outgoing HTTP call or two separate attempts? can you paste the outgoing header debug?

sam: same call. deploy-bot logged:
[deploy-bot] outgoing POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate headers: Authorization: Bearer abc123, Authorization: Bearer abc123, Content-Type: application/json

mira: repro steps: package.json with "type": "module" and exports: {"./runtime": {"import": "./dist/runtime.mjs","require":"./dist/runtime.cjs"}}, then worker does `import { RedwoodClient } from './runtime'`. esbuild sometimes inlines both runtime.mjs and runtime.cjs and both run their top-level side-effects.

angel: that pattern is known to confuse bundlers in edge contexts. When both variants are included we hit double-init. Our auth middleware is supposed to be lazy, but we still have a top-level attach for older CJS flows. Combined equals duplicate header.

kevin: immediate mitigation: make top-level init idempotent and remove side-effectful header attach. Prefer request-time injection of Authorization. Add a global guard like `if (globalThis.__redwood_init_done) return; globalThis.__redwood_init_done = true;`.

mira: I hacked that locally and it fixes it. Also we should update sampleapp-edge to explicitly import the ESM worker build (dist/worker.mjs) in the example to avoid ambiguous resolution.

angel: TS editors also get confused with conditional exports. We should add an explicit `types` entry in exports so IDEs pick the right .d.ts and people don't see conflicting overloads.

kevin: long-term: revisit package exports layout so bundlers pick a single runtime for edge targets. Short-term: add an SDK safety shim that detects double-init, update sampleapp-edge README with a recommended wrangler/esbuild config, and add a Miniflare smoke test in CI to catch regressions.

sam: for immediate unblock I changed sampleapp-edge to import the built mjs directly and pinned wrangler to esbuild target es2020; that prevented dual-chunk bundling for me.

mira: I'll open a PR with the init-guard + README change + explicit worker example. Will follow up with the CI smoke test PR adding a Miniflare assertion that outgoing requests contain at most one Authorization header.

ci-bot: queued: sampleapp-edge/miniflare-smoke-test (optional).

kevin: solid. Tag me on the PR, I'll review the init guard and the docs. Also please add a short note in the "Edge runtimes" devex doc about avoiding ambiguous conditional exports and how to force a single ESM bundle for workers.

angel: I'll work up the tiny SDK shim and a one-paragraph entry for the devex guide. We should also include the exact worker import pattern: `import { RedwoodClient } from './dist/runtime.mjs'` and sample wrangler.toml snippet.

sam: thanks all, this saved a lot of time. :relieved:
